title: Cancer cells are not more selfish; they have smaller selves

fields.label: Label
fields.value: Cancer cells are not more selfish; they have smaller selves

fields.label: Statement
fields.value: On the cognitive light cone model of cancer, in which the 'cognitive light cone' is the spatiotemporal size of the homeodynamic goal states a system can pursue, cancer is a pathological rolling back to small cell-level goals: cancer cells are not more selfish but have smaller selves, treating the rest of the body as external environment.

fields.label: Work
fields.value: The Multiscale Wisdom of the Body: Collective Intelligence as a Tractable Interface for Next-Generation Biomedicine

fields.label: Chapter
fields.value: Levin M 2025, The Multiscale Wisdom of the Body: Collective Intelligence as a Tractable Interface for Next-Generation Biomedicine › Cancer and the Scaling of the Self

fields.label: Quotation
fields.value: But more specifically, the cognitive light cone model suggests that cancer cells are not more selfish; they just have smaller selves.

fields.label: Assumptions
fields.value: Levin M, “The Multiscale Wisdom of the Body: Collective Intelligence as a Tractable Interface for Next-Generation Biomedicine”, BioEssays : news and reviews in molecular, cellular and developmental biology (2025), doi:10.1002/bies.202400196; section “Cancer and the Scaling of the Self”. Scope: Cancer in multicellular animals

fields.label: Assessment
fields.value: GPT-5.6 Sol on levin-2025-wisdom-13: not-empirically-resolvable, resolvability 0.21

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: Cancer-cell spatial and temporal dependencies can be measured, but calling them smaller selves is a conceptual redescription. As stated, no observation chooses this framing over standard cell-autonomy mechanisms.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: No independent measure is supplied that distinguishes a smaller Self from increased selfishness or ordinary loss of tissue-level regulation in the same cancer-cell behaviours.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
The rival descriptions predict the same proliferation and cooperation phenotypes.

Cognitive light cone and Self size are not operationally independent.

fields.label: Dimension scores
fields.value:
analysis feasibility: 0.35
operationalizability: 0.15
data existence: 0.3
discriminating power: 0.1
data adequacy: 0.15

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: The cognitive-light-cone wording restates cancer as a retreat from tissue-scale goals to cell-scale goals. Gap-junction loss, autonomous proliferation, and disregard of tissue boundaries are the same facts under a non-cognitive description. No existing observation would show that cancer cells are not more selfish but instead have smaller selves.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: The spatial scale of tissue-level homeostasis can be measured, but a smaller homeostatic domain does not distinguish smaller selves from loss of coupling, and it does not decide whether cells are less selfish.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Any isolation phenotype can be described either as a smaller self or as failed multicellular control.

Self size and selfishness are not separately measurable in tumor data.
